audit.whatIsWrong: The entire content layer describes a champion Aurelion Sol has not been for years. It talks about his 'orbit', 'stars', 'star-grazing', an 'orbit's dead zone', 'Starsurge' and 'Voice of Light'. None of those exist in the kit: his abilities are Cosmic Creator, Breath of Light, Astral Flight, Singularity and Falling Star / The Skies Descend. Nine separate fields were written against the wrong kit.
audit.why: 'Stay inside his orbit's dead zone instead of at max range' tells the reader to walk to melee against a champion whose black hole executes them there. It is not merely stale, it is dangerous advice.
audit.corrected: Breath of Light is a 750-range channel on 3s that gains bonus damage for each second it is aimed directly at you. Singularity is a flat 12s black hole that pulls toward a centre which executes below a health percentage. Falling Star is a 1250-range stun on 120s at rank 1, upgrading to The Skies Descend with enough Stardust.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit P/Q/W/E/R text, ranges, cooldowns)

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: Aurora wins 47.81% but the content chart gave her all seven stages. The full layer's own sides read Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Skill/Skill/Aurelion Sol/Aurelion Sol.
audit.why: A sub-50% matchup cannot be a clean sweep at every stage, and the full layer's shape matches the kit — Aurora's 900 range beats his 750 early, and Cosmic Creator's permanent Stardust upgrades tilt the later stages to him.
audit.corrected: content win[] moved onto the full layer's sides as one atomic group, whys[] rewritten to match each verdict.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].side and phases[6].side both read Aurelion Sol while their whys described Aurora's Luden's spike and Aurora warping teamfights — the row and the sentence under it gave opposite answers.
audit.why: Those two stages are his because Cosmic Creator converts every damaging ability into Stardust that permanently improves the rest of his kit, and enough Stardust upgrades Falling Star into The Skies Descend.
audit.corrected: Both whys rewritten in the same proposal to argue the verdict above them; the sides were left where they were.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit P and R text)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and described Astral Flight as purely 'his reposition and escape'. Riot's text says that while flying, Breath of Light has no cooldown and no maximum channel duration and deals increased damage.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 3, and a player who reads Astral Flight as an escape will walk under a flying Aurelion Sol into his strongest damage state.
audit.corrected: Astral Flight 22s at rank 1 and it is a damage window as much as an escape; Singularity a flat 12s; Falling Star 120s at rank 1; Breath of Light a flat 3s.
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit W text and cooldowns)

audit.whatIsWrong: Two mechanics that decide when you may be low near him were absent: Singularity's centre executes enemies below a health percentage, and its damage is percent-health, so resistances are not the answer. 'Twin Drift' also appears as an Aurora ability in spikes[0].text and early, and it is not one.
audit.why: An execute threshold changes what a health bar means; the page treated his damage as ordinary poke.
audit.corrected: Track the number, not the bar, and never finish a fight standing on the black hole. Aurora's leap is Across the Veil (W).
sources: champ-data/_kits (brief enemyKit E text and flags)

audit.whatIsWrong: The wave section was the same template used on every other matchup and said nothing about him.
audit.why: Breath of Light is a flat 3s costing 35 mana at rank 1, so shoving does not tax him the way it taxes a burst mage.
audit.corrected: Wave text rewritten around his cheap 3s clear and around Falling Star's 1250 range while your hop is down.

notes:
This matchup's content layer was written against the pre-rework Aurelion Sol — orbit, stars, star-grazing, dead zone, Starsurge, Voice of Light. Nine fields, including every spike, every why and four of the six wants. It is the largest single block of wrong-kit text I found. The worst of it was wants.you[0], which instructed the reader to close to melee 'inside his orbit's dead zone' — against a champion whose black hole pulls inward toward an execute.

Level chart: the packet itself flagged it (47.81% win rate against a 7-0 Aurora chart). I moved content win[3..6] onto the full layer's existing sides — Skill, Skill, Aurelion Sol, Aurelion Sol — as one group; win[0..2] already read Aurora and match. phases[5].why and phases[6].why were the contradicting-row defect and were rewritten to argue his side rather than moved.

Derived-flag caution: Aurora's R carries a 'hardCC' flag while Riot's own text for it says only damages and slows. Because the two disagree I did NOT write anything about Aurora interrupting Breath of Light or The Skies Descend with her ultimate, even though his Q and W both carry the 'channel — interruptible' flag and that would have been the most useful line in the matchup. If someone can confirm Aurora's R applies a knock-up or stun on the shockwave, that interrupt is worth adding to breakdown.cooldowns.

SuspectNames: 'Save Between Worlds' is a real name, so the near-miss flag is a false positive — but the line named an ability the enemy does not have (Voice of Light), so it was replaced anyway.
